sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Test for text splitting safety
sections.what: Checks that splitting claims into pages keeps every character, respects the size and item limits, never splits an emoji pair, and rebuilds short text exactly.
sections.why: Likely reason: lost or broken text in a deck would be hard for the owner to notice, so the test guards it.
sections.watch_out: Passing this test proves text is kept intact, not that slides look right.

summary: A automated test that checks text splitting across pages keeps every character and never breaks an emoji pair.
purpose: Protects against lost words, lost spaces or broken characters when long text is split across slides.
why: Reason inferred from the test name and checks: the splitting must never drop or corrupt text.
how: It builds two long claims, one with plain text and one with an emoji and repeated spaces, splits them into pages, then checks that joining the pieces gives back the original text exactly, that every page stays within the size and item limits, that no page starts or ends with half an emoji, and that a short split case also rebuilds the original.
inputs: Two sample claims with text and ids, and a sample string with an emoji near a split point.
outputs: A pass or fail result from the Node test runner.
risks: This only checks text. It does not prove that the slides look right or fit on the page.
debug: If the test fails, first look at the first assertion, which compares joined text. Then check textFragments and paginateClaims in contentPagination.ts. The test was not run in this review, so its current result is unknown.
